summary: OpenAPI response validation runs unconditionally on every response, hot path included — gate it and amend ADR-028
description:
### Finding (architecture review R1, 2026-07-25)

`shared/go/contract.responseValidated` wraps **every** handler in all five services. For each request it:

1. buffers the whole response into an `httptest.ResponseRecorder`,
2. re-routes the request against the OpenAPI document (`router.FindRoute`),
3. re-parses the recorded body and walks it against the response schema (`openapi3filter.ValidateResponse`),
4. copies headers and body out to the real `ResponseWriter`.

There is no toggle. This runs on `POST /holds` and the three transitions under on-sale load, i.e. exactly the path `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` holds to a p99 ≤ 1s SLO. It is the largest self-inflicted cost standing against the project's stated scalability assumption, and it is one config knob away from being paid only where it earns its keep.

Two smaller defects in the same function:

- it calls `context.Background()` for validation, so a drift error is logged **outside** the request trace — the one place you would want `trace_id`;
- the recorder discards `http.Flusher`/`http.Hijacker`, so no handler behind it can ever stream.

### Not in scope

**Request** validation stays unconditional. It is a trust boundary and its cost is bounded by the request body, which is small on these routes. Only the response side moves.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Response validation is switchable via `runtimecfg` (with the rest of the bounded-resource policy), defaulted **on** for dev/CI/smoke.
- [ ] ADR-028 is amended to state where fail-closed applies and why the placement changed. Semantics where enabled are untouched.
- [ ] `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` is run with validation on and off; the p99 delta for hold/finalize/confirm is **recorded as a number** in `docs/evidence/`. If the delta is negligible, say so and keep validation everywhere — that outcome closes the ticket honestly.
- [ ] With validation enabled, TKT-108's mask-body detection still passes.
- [ ] The validator runs on the request context, so a drift log carries `trace_id`.
- [ ] `make check` green.

objective.note: OpenAPI response validation currently runs unconditionally on every response in every service, including inventory's claim path under on-sale load. Make it configurable so the contract guarantee is paid for where it has value (dev/CI/smoke) and not on the production hot path.

scope.note: IN: an explicit enable/sample switch for response validation in shared/go/contract, defaulted on for dev/CI/smoke; the ADR-028 amendment saying where fail-closed applies; passing the request context into the validator instead of context.Background(); a measured before/after on the on-sale load test. OUT: request validation (stays unconditional — it is a trust boundary); removing the guarantee anywhere it is currently proven; any change to the drift semantics where validation IS enabled.

uncertainties.note: Whether production runs it fully off or sampled at a low rate. Sampling keeps a live drift signal at a fraction of the cost but complicates the fail-closed contract (a sampled request fails closed, an unsampled one does not — two behaviours for one endpoint). The plan decides against the measured delta; both satisfy the COS.

dependencies.note: None. shared/go/contract is consumed by all five services but the change is additive (a config knob with the current behaviour as the dev/CI default).

approach.note: Config through runtimecfg, alongside the other bounded-resource policy, not a bespoke env read per service. Keep ADR-028's fail-closed semantics EXACTLY as they are wherever validation is enabled — this ticket changes where it runs, not what it does. The evidence for the change is the load test, not reasoning: measure with it on and off.

first_slice.note: The knob + the ADR-028 amendment + the measurement. If the measured delta turns out to be negligible, that is a valid outcome — record it in the ADR and keep validation on everywhere; the ticket is then a documentation and context-propagation fix. Do not force the change against the measurement.

success.note: COS: (1) response validation is switchable, defaulted on in dev/CI/smoke; (2) ADR-028 states where fail-closed applies and why the placement changed; (3) smoke/onsale_load_test.go is run in both configurations and the p99 delta is recorded in the ticket and in docs/evidence — a number, not an estimate; (4) with validation enabled, TKT-108's mask-body detection still passes (the laundered-status learning still holds); (5) the validator runs on the request context so drift errors carry trace_id; (6) make check green.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-028 (the decision being amended — placement, not semantics), ADR-009 (contract-first is the reason the guarantee exists at all), ADR-004 (the read path this sits in front of). Learning: docs/learnings/2026-07-21-test-validator-downstream-of-production-wrap-sees-laundered-statuses.md — the mask body is the detectable artifact, not the status; and docs/learnings/2026-07-25-coarse-observables-pass-the-broken-build.md — a coarse observable will not show this delta, the load test's p99 will.

binding.rule: A response that drifts from the served OpenAPI contract fails closed: the drifted payload never reaches the client, and the violation is logged with the operation coordinates.

APIs are contract-first: the OpenAPI spec is the source of truth, served by the service at /openapi.yaml and checked for drift in the gate; domain events use a versioned platform envelope (id, type==subject, occurred_at, schema, data) published to JetStream with acks (never fire-and-forget), with a deterministic envelope id so retried/raced emissions de-duplicate.
Public reads declare volatility-tiered TTLs; the read path is cache-first, and each tier has exactly one cache owner so staleness never stacks.
Reservation claims are decided inside a single Postgres transaction under a row lock; no external lock manager. Oversell is bounded by the database, not by application coordination.

---

# TKT-125 execution plan

## 1. Configuration and middleware design

Use one boolean switch; do not introduce sampling machinery.

- Environment variable: `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED`
- Type: boolean parsed with `strconv.ParseBool`
- Default: `true`
- Invalid values: fail service startup with an error naming the variable but not its value
- Development, CI, and smoke: remain enabled through the default
- Production recommendation: disable completely if the measurement shows a material cost; if the delta is negligible, leave it enabled everywhere as required by the ticket’s decision rule

Add an unexported `boolean(name string, fallback bool) (bool, error)` helper in `shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg.go`, following the existing `duration` and `integer` helpers.

Extend the existing HTTP policy rather than adding a separate configuration read:

```go
type HTTP struct {
    ReadHeaderTimeout       time.Duration
    ReadTimeout             time.Duration
    WriteTimeout            time.Duration
    IdleTimeout             time.Duration
    ValidateOpenAPIResponses bool
}
```

`HTTPFromEnv()` reads `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED`, defaulting it to `true`. `HTTP.Apply` continues applying only `http.Server` fields; each service consumes `ValidateOpenAPIResponses` while constructing its API router.

Thread the value explicitly through these signatures:

```go
// shared/go/contract/http.go
func RequestValidator(
    spec []byte,
    next http.Handler,
    log *slog.Logger,
    validateResponses bool,
) (http.Handler, error)

func RequestValidatorWithErrorHandler(
    spec []byte,
    next http.Handler,
    log *slog.Logger,
    validateResponses bool,
    errorHandler func(http.ResponseWriter, string, int),
) (http.Handler, error)

func ResponseValidator(
    spec []byte,
    next http.Handler,
    log *slog.Logger,
    validateResponses bool,
) (http.Handler, error)

func requestValidator(
    spec []byte,
    next http.Handler,
    log *slog.Logger,
    validateResponses bool,
    errorHandler func(http.ResponseWriter, string, int),
) (http.Handler, error)
```

Change the service router seams to:

```go
// inventory, commerce, payments, access
func (s *Server) Router(log *slog.Logger, validateResponses bool) http.Handler

// catalog
func NewRouter(s *Server, validateResponses bool) (http.Handler, error)
```

Update the five production call sites:

- `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go`: `Router(log, httpConfig.ValidateOpenAPIResponses)`
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go`: same
- `services/payments/cmd/payments/main.go`: same
- `services/access/cmd/access/main.go`: same
- `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/main.go`: `NewRouter(..., httpConfig.ValidateOpenAPIResponses)`

All unit and smoke-test router construction passes `true` explicitly. This is intentional: it keeps ADR-030’s catalog unit coverage gate behind the real response validator and makes disabling it in a test a visible choice.

`load(spec)` should still run at router construction when response validation is disabled. This preserves startup-time OpenAPI loading and validation; only the per-response buffering, route lookup, and schema walk are removed.

Within `requestValidator`:

1. Always construct and install the request validator.
2. If response validation is enabled, wrap `next` with `responseValidated`.
3. If disabled, give `next` directly to the request validator.

Within `ResponseValidator`, choose between `responseValidated` and direct `next` after loading the spec.

When the switch is off:

- Request validation remains unconditional.
- Responses, including drifting bodies and undocumented statuses, pass through unchanged.
- No generic contract 500 is substituted.
- No response-drift log is emitted.
- There is no runtime response-conformance or fail-closed guarantee for that request.

When enabled, status, headers, body, structured log fields, undocumented-status handling, and the generic 500 remain byte-for-byte equivalent to HEAD.

## 2. Sampling decision

Recommend fully off in production rather than sampled validation, provided the measured delta is material.

Fully off has the simplest contract: production responses are never buffered or runtime-validated, while dev/CI/smoke retain deterministic fail-closed validation. Its cost is the loss of live drift detection; a regression missed by the exercised gate coverage can reach clients.

Sampling retains a partial live signal and pays roughly the sampling fraction of the validation cost, but introduces two observable behaviours for the same endpoint:

- Sampled requests fail closed.
- Unsampled requests return the same drifting payload.

It also adds rate configuration, selection logic, deterministic-testing concerns, and incomplete diagnostics. A rare production drift could alternate between 500 and a nominal success, complicating client behaviour and incident analysis. That complexity is not justified for this testbed.

Do not add a rate, RNG, hash sampler, or enum in this ticket. The knob remains boolean.

If the measured delta is negligible, follow the ticket’s explicit branch: keep validation fully on in production as well. Record that result rather than forcing either full-off or sampling.

## 3. Strict TDD sequence

### Slice A: runtime configuration

Add tests first in `shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg_test.go`:

- `TestHTTPDefaultsResponseValidationOn`
  - Removes the variable from the test environment.
  - Calls `HTTPFromEnv`.
  - Asserts `ValidateOpenAPIResponses == true`.

- `TestHTTPCanDisableResponseValidation`
  - Sets `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED=false`.
  - Asserts the returned field is false.

- Extend `TestInvalidConfiguration` with a boolean case.
  - Sets a non-boolean value.
  - Asserts `HTTPFromEnv` fails and identifies `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED`.

Run and observe red:

```sh
(cd shared/go && go test ./runtimecfg)
```

The initial red should be the missing field/helper or the unimplemented environment parsing. Implement only this slice, then rerun green.

### Slice B: shared contract behaviour

Add tests first in `shared/go/contract/http_test.go` against the new explicit boolean parameter:

- `TestResponseValidationDisabledPassesDriftUnmodified`
  - Builds a documented route whose handler returns a drifting body.
  - Disables response validation.
  - Asserts the handler’s original status, headers, and exact body reach the client.
  - Asserts no drift log is emitted.

- `TestRequestValidationRemainsEnabledWhenResponseValidationIsDisabled`
  - Disables response validation but sends an invalid request body.
  - Asserts the request is rejected and the handler is never called.

- `TestResponseValidationEnabledPreservesFailClosedResponse`
  - Enables validation and emits the same drift.
  - Asserts exactly:
    - status `500`;
    - `Content-Type: application/json`;
    - `Cache-Control: no-store`;
    - body `{"error":"response violates OpenAPI contract"}\n`;
    - the existing structured `method`, `path`, original `status`, and `error` fields.
  - This pins ADR-028 semantics against accidental changes while moving the placement.

- Retain and adapt `TestUndocumentedResponseStatusIsRejected`.
  - Pass `true`.
  - Continue proving `IncludeResponseStatus` behaviour.

- Retain and adapt both `ResponseValidator` tests.
  - Test enabled drift rejection and enabled valid/undocumented-route passthrough.
  - Add the disabled drifting-response case to the response-only catalog seam.

- `TestResponseValidationUsesRequestContext`
  - Add an unexported function type accepted by `responseValidated`, equivalent to:

    ```go
    type validateResponseFunc func(context.Context, *openapi3filter.ResponseValidationInput) error
    ```

  - Production callers pass `openapi3filter.ValidateResponse`.
  - The test supplies a fake validator, puts a sentinel and an active OpenTelemetry span in the request context, returns a validation error, and asserts:
    - the fake received the request context rather than `context.Background()`;
    - the emitted log contains the span’s `trace_id`.

This injection is preferable to a mutable package-level test hook and remains concurrency-safe.

HEAD already calls `logger.ErrorContext(r.Context(), ...)`, so a trace-only test would pass without detecting the `ValidateResponse(context.Background(), ...)` defect. The fake validator assertion is what makes the context test meaningful and red before the implementation change.

Run and observe red:

```sh
(cd shared/go && go test ./contract)
```

Implement the boolean branch and change:

```go
openapi3filter.ValidateResponse(context.Background(), input)
```

to validation with the request context. Rerun the package green.

### Slice C: service wiring and ADR-030 protection

Change the router signatures and first update all tests to pass `true`. Compilation failures identify any missed call site.

For catalog, add a focused wiring test beside `TestRuntimeResponseDriftFailsClosed` in `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go`:

- Construct the same deliberately invalid negative-price fixture through `NewRouter(..., false)`.
- Assert the original response passes through rather than becoming the ADR-028 500.
- Keep `TestRuntimeResponseDriftFailsClosed` using `true`.

Refactor `newEnv` in `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` only as far as necessary to provide an explicit enabled/disabled constructor; its normal path must remain enabled.

Run:

```sh
(cd services/catalog && go test ./internal/api)
(cd services/inventory && go test ./internal/api)
(cd services/commerce && go test ./internal/api)
(cd services/payments && go test ./internal/api)
(cd services/access && go test ./internal/api)
```

The unfiltered catalog run is required because its `TestMain` coverage gate is intentionally skipped under `-run`.

The catalog run also exercises TKT-108’s mask-body detection in `env.validateResponse`: any normal enabled test that receives `response violates OpenAPI contract` must still fail hard.

## 4. Context and streaming defects

Replace the validation call’s `context.Background()` with the request context through the injected validation function. Keep `logger.ErrorContext(r.Context(), ...)`.

The streaming/Hijacker defect should be split into a separate ticket.

Reason: fail-closed response validation requires retaining the entire response until its status, headers, and body have been accepted. A real flush sends bytes before validation can decide to replace the response with a 500, and a hijacked connection is no longer an HTTP response the middleware can validate. Preserving true streaming semantics while retaining ADR-028 fail-closed behaviour is therefore a policy decision, not an adapter fix.

For TKT-125:

- Enabled mode remains buffered and does not promise streaming or hijacking.
- Disabled mode passes the original `ResponseWriter` directly, naturally restoring its optional interfaces.
- Amend ADR-028’s buffering consequence to state this explicitly.
- Open a follow-up only when a streaming/hijacking route exists, with a route-level exclusion or a different validation contract decided then.

## 5. Measurement

Use the existing full NFR profile, not the advisory gate profile. The relevant values are the `nfr-3000pm` stage’s hold, finalize, and confirm p99s.

Build once:

```sh
make build-gate-linux build-ts
mkdir -p docs/evidence/TKT-125
```

Run enabled:

```sh
OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true \
ONSALE_PROFILE=full \
ONSALE_REPORT="$PWD/docs/evidence/TKT-125/response-validation-on.json" \
SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT=40m \
./scripts/smoke.sh
```

Run disabled on the same idle host and commit:

```sh
OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED=false \
ONSALE_PROFILE=full \
ONSALE_REPORT="$PWD/docs/evidence/TKT-125/response-validation-off.json" \
SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT=40m \
./scripts/smoke.sh
```

Each invocation receives a clean isolated Compose stack through `scripts/smoke.sh`. `compose.yaml` must expose `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED` through the shared `x-go-service` environment so the shell override reaches all five services.

Extract from each report:

```sh
jq '.stages[] | select(.name == "nfr-3000pm") |
    {hold_p99_ms, finalize_p99_ms, confirm_p99_ms}' \
    docs/evidence/TKT-125/response-validation-on.json \
    docs/evidence/TKT-125/response-validation-off.json
```

Create `docs/evidence/TKT-125/README.md` containing:

- commit SHA and host details;
- exact commands;
- confirmation that both runs completed with zero drops/client errors/server errors in the NFR window;
- a table for hold, finalize, and confirm with:
  - validation-on p99 in milliseconds;
  - validation-off p99 in milliseconds;
  - absolute delta `on - off` in milliseconds;
  - percentage delta `(on - off) / off × 100`;
- the operational conclusion.

If the first pair is close enough that host noise could determine the decision, run two more alternating pairs, retain the additional JSON reports with numbered suffixes, and compare medians. Do not describe a one-pair near-zero result as causal evidence.

If the delta is negligible:

- Keep `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true` as the production policy.
- Retain the switch, default-on behaviour, request-context fix, tests, and evidence.
- Amend ADR-028 to say the runtime placement was measured and deliberately retained everywhere.
- Do not introduce sampling merely to exercise the knob.

If the delta is material:

- Recommend production set the variable to `false`.
- Keep dev, CI, `make check`, and normal smoke runs at the default `true`.
- Record that production has no runtime response fail-closed guarantee.

The validation-off measurement is performance evidence only; it does not replace the normal validation-on `make check`.

## 6. ADR-028 amendment

Amend `docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md` after measurement so its conclusion contains the actual numbers.

Update these sections:

- **Status**
  - Record the TKT-125 amendment and date.

- **Context**
  - Replace the unconditional “every service response” claim.
  - Describe the recorder, per-request `FindRoute`, body decode/schema walk, and on-sale hold-transition placement.
  - Reference the TKT-125 evidence.

- **Possible Solutions**
  - Preserve the historical fail-closed versus pass-through decision.
  - Add placement alternatives: fully enabled, production-off with gate-on, and sampled.
  - Record why sampling was rejected.

- **Decision**
  - Request validation remains unconditional.
  - `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED` controls only response validation.
  - Default is enabled.
  - Wherever enabled, existing fail-closed semantics are unchanged.
  - State the measured production setting: off if material, otherwise retained on.

- **Consequences**
  - Enabled mode still buffers and cannot promise streaming/hijacking.
  - Disabled mode has no runtime response-schema rejection or drift log.
  - Gate-time checks remain enabled and deterministic.
  - Record the availability/diagnostic trade-off supported by the measured p99 deltas.

Apply ADR-021’s claim discipline explicitly:

- This is an honest-implementation consistency control, not tamper-evidence.
- When enabled, it guarantees only that a response which reaches this middleware and fails the committed schema/status validation is replaced before reaching the client.
- It does not guarantee semantic correctness of schema-valid data.
- It does not constrain an adversary who can change service code or configuration, disable the switch, replace the OpenAPI document, or produce malicious but schema-valid data.
- When disabled, there is no runtime response-contract guarantee.
- The gate guarantee covers exercised test paths only:
  - catalog’s per-operation obligation is unit-level with a fake store under ADR-030;
  - inventory, commerce, payments, and access use the smoke coverage gate;
  - the coverage gates do not prove every documented status or every production data state.

## 7. Final verification

Run the focused tests during each TDD slice, then the normal enabled gate:

```sh
make check
```

Confirm:

- response validation is on in the normal smoke stack;
- TKT-108 mask-body detection still passes in the unfiltered catalog suite;
- `smoke/contract_validation_test.go` continues validating exercised real-stack responses;
- the validation-off load run is not used as the gate result;
- no OpenAPI document changed and no generated file drift was introduced.

No browser form verification is required because this ticket changes only Go HTTP middleware and configuration.

## 8. Files touched

| File | Reason |
|---|---|
| `shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg.go` | Add the default-on HTTP policy field and boolean environment parser. |
| `shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg_test.go` | Pin default-on, explicit-off, and malformed-value behaviour. |
| `shared/go/contract/http.go` | Gate response wrapping, preserve unconditional request validation, and pass request context into response validation. |
| `shared/go/contract/http_test.go` | Pin disabled passthrough, enabled byte identity, unconditional request validation, and request-context/trace behaviour. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go` | Accept and forward the response-validation policy. |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` | Same. |
| `services/payments/internal/api/server.go` | Same. |
| `services/access/internal/api/server.go` | Same while preserving the custom request error handler. |
| `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` | Gate catalog’s response-only wrapper while retaining catalog’s request validator. |
| `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go` | Pass `HTTPFromEnv` policy into `Router`. |
| `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` | Same. |
| `services/payments/cmd/payments/main.go` | Same. |
| `services/access/cmd/access/main.go` | Same. |
| `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/main.go` | Pass the policy into `NewRouter`. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/server_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/seat_handler_smoke_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/server_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/payments/internal/api/server_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/payments/internal/api/psp_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/access/internal/api/server_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/access/internal/api/server_smoke_test.go` | Pass enabled explicitly. |
| `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` | Keep the normal catalog environment explicitly enabled and support the focused disabled wiring test. |
| `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go` | Pin both enabled fail-closed wiring and disabled passthrough without weakening ADR-030. |
| `compose.yaml` | Propagate the default-on environment variable to all Go services. |
| `docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md` | Amend placement, guarantees, sampling decision, evidence, and streaming limitation. |

`smoke/onsale_load_test.go`, `scripts/smoke.sh`, the Makefile, OpenAPI documents, and generated API files should not need modification.

## 9. Risks and failure modes

- **Catalog coverage silently loses its validator.** Mitigate by passing `true` explicitly from `newEnv`, retaining `TestRuntimeResponseDriftFailsClosed`, adding the disabled wiring test separately, and running the unfiltered catalog suite.
- **TKT-108 laundering detection is bypassed.** Keep normal catalog tests enabled and preserve the exact generic mask body used by `env.validateResponse`.
- **Smoke’s contract guarantee is weakened by environment leakage.** `compose.yaml` defaults the variable to true; CI and the final `make check` must run without the off override. Treat the off run only as measurement.
- **The load harness performs only partial transition-body checks.** `loadtest.ValidTransitionBody` checks the target status and currently relies on middleware for full shape validation. This is acceptable for the controlled off measurement but is not a replacement production contract guarantee.
- **A missed router call site defaults to false accidentally.** Avoid optional/variadic parameters and update every call site explicitly; compilation should fail until all are handled.
- **Disabled mode changes more than CPU cost.** Direct writes restore the real writer’s interface and remove buffering/header replay. The passthrough test must assert original status, headers, and bytes so this is deliberate.
- **A malformed boolean is silently treated as false.** Fail startup instead of accepting an invalid value.
- **Near-zero results are dominated by host noise.** Use the full NFR stage on the same host and commit; repeat alternating pairs before declaring negligible.
- **The gate is overclaimed.** Catalog uses fake-store unit coverage, smoke coverage counts an operation after any documented 2xx, and neither proves unexercised statuses or schema-valid semantic correctness. Preserve those limits in ADR-028.
- **Streaming is “fixed” by exposing `Flush` through the buffer.** That would still not stream to the client and could violate fail-closed ordering. Leave enabled-mode streaming/hijacking unsupported and split the policy decision.
- **Sampling sneaks in later through a numeric interpretation of the boolean.** Keep the accepted values boolean and reject a rate; sampling requires a new ADR amendment and contract.
